themes.name: Integration of Sustainability into Academic Curricula
themes.definition: Efforts and approaches to embed Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into the curriculum, courses, and programs at higher education institutions, often involving interdisciplinary and program-level design.
evidence: [MarNou_2025] explores how the program integrates interdisciplinary learning, global–local connectivity, and sustainability competencies.
[CasDes_2022] aims at shedding light on the curriculum design process of an education module called ‘Public Administration and Sustainability’
[SarEmb_2025] Integrating the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) into marketing education

themes.name: Innovative Pedagogical Methods for ESD
themes.definition: Use of specific teaching and learning strategies such as problem-based learning, game-based learning, experiential learning, and participatory methods to promote sustainability education and engage students.
evidence: [WilPro_2018] the instrument of learning diaries or the implementation of problem-based learning modules
[EmbPro_2018] game-based learning and teaching for business sustainability
[VerEng_2023] interdisciplinary teamwork skills through project-based learning

themes.name: Whole-Institution Approaches to Sustainability
themes.definition: Comprehensive, university-wide strategies that integrate sustainability across governance, operations, teaching, research, and community engagement, following a holistic or whole-institution approach.
evidence: [SchSus_2018] whole institutional approach and sustainability-oriented organizational development
[HemSus_2021] whole-institution approach with their overall sustainability concept
[RatSus_2017] degrees of institutionalization for sustainability at German higher education institutions

themes.name: Development of Sustainability Competences
themes.definition: Focus on equipping students and educators with the knowledge, skills, values, and competences necessary for addressing sustainability challenges, often aligned with ESD frameworks.
evidence: [VerEng_2023] equipping students with competencies-knowledge, skills, and values-that will engage and empower them to contribute to sustainable development
[SivEng_2016] holistic sustainability competences
[CasMov_2023] ESD competences feature in the educators’ teaching experiences

themes.name: Case Studies and Contextual Implementations
themes.definition: Research and examples that present specific instances of ESD implementation in different countries, regions, or institutions, highlighting local adaptations, challenges, and practices.
evidence: [CasDes_2022] a longitudinal case study from the Maltese islands
[KhaCli_2021] Climate change education in Ukrainian universities
[YanHig_2022] describe how the SDGs are integrated into HEIs in China

themes.name: Barriers to ESD Implementation
themes.definition: Identification of obstacles and challenges faced in integrating ESD into higher education, including lack of resources, resistance to change, institutional barriers, and guidance gaps.
evidence: [EspEmb_2025] barriers to the implementation of ESD, including a lack of detailed guidance, resistance to change and lack of financial resources
[SchSus_2018] barriers for sustainability-orientated transformation at higher education institutions
[KhaCli_2021] functional factors ... that promote or hinder CCESD’s embedment

themes.name: Role of Educators as Change Agents
themes.definition: Emphasis on the critical role of lecturers and teachers in promoting sustainability, often through professional development, change projects, and as facilitators of transformative education.
evidence: [MurTra_2018] promote the role of lecturers as 'change agents' for sustainability
[KhaCha_2021] Change Project Approach for reorienting university teaching
[WilPro_2018] demands high standards of the lecturers

themes.name: Frameworks and Models for ESD Integration
themes.definition: Use of structured frameworks, models, or tools to guide the implementation and assessment of ESD in higher education curricula and institutions, providing systematic approaches.
evidence: [MarNou_2025] 4Cs framework—curriculum, campus, community, and culture
[SarEmb_2025] LIFT Framework (Learn, Innovate, Facilitate, Transform)
[GraAn _2023] architectural teaching and learning framework

data.meta_observations: The abstracts predominantly use case study methodologies, with a strong focus on practical implementation and sharing experiences across different countries and disciplines. There is a recurring emphasis on holistic and interdisciplinary approaches, and many studies aim to inform policy or practice. However, several abstracts note missing elements such as results or quantitative data, which may limit evidence-based conclusions.
data.grounding_notes: All evidence quotes are verbatim from the provided abstracts, adhering to anti-hallucination rules. Some themes overlap (e.g., curriculum integration and pedagogical methods), but they are kept distinct based on explicit terminology in the data. Frequency classifications are based on the number of articles explicitly mentioning each theme within this batch. Confidence is high due to direct textual support.
